name: Breathe Right
beta:
Start on the left flank of the small ledgy boulder; steady, sequential moves on big holds lead to a relaxing stretch.

Near the top bear a little right through a brownish band, then step over a small roof and reach the chains.
overview: Big holds climb a section needing precise sequencing, with another chance to recover on big holds. The line angles slightly rightward through a brown band and tackles a brief roof before the chains.

current.area_walk_in: From the parking lot, follow the trail system toward the Motherlode and take the left-hand fork.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Leftmost line of this stretch of cliff, up from the near end of a squat, shelved boulder

name: Brontosaurus
beta:
Work up a rock chute to a stance under a little roof; slot in protection, then launch across to the crack for some very good-feeling hand jams.

Stay focused on the thinner stretch near the top.
overview: A very enjoyable hand-width crack inside the dihedral. Climb a rock chute to a perch beneath a little roof, set a piece, then leap into the crack for outstanding jams; stay sharp for the thin part higher up.

current.area_walk_in: A switchbacking trail climbs the hillside and ends directly below the conspicuous pinnacle holding The Arrowhead.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Brother Stair
beta: Mostly tracks a blunt arete, then breaks rightward at the very top to reach the anchors.
overview: Mostly tracks a blunt arete, bailing rightward near the end.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About twenty feet along from where the path meets the cliff, just around an arete

name: Buff the Wood
beta:
Work up to the small finger crack roughly fifteen feet up, clip, and shake out. Then shift right along crimps, deadpointing across to the crimp rail.

Fire off to a jug, continue up the wall to a pocketed section, make a few big moves and clip the chains.
overview: Bouldery moves lead into a thin finger split where the first clip is made. Following a pause, the climbing drifts rightward across crimps with a lunge to a rail, and a pocketed headwall with big reaches completes it.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Next to Stain on its right-hand side, below a small finger-wide split roughly 15 ft off the ground

name: Burlier's Bane
beta: Begin under the big hueco; pinch holds and deceptive sucker jugs lead to the anchors.
overview: A short pump up pinch holds and deceptive jugs, starting underneath a big hueco and continuing to the lower-off.

current.area_walk_in: Walk toward the right from Madness Cave to reach a lower, less steep wall holding many lines. The first line met is The Sauce, beside a large tree that grows against the cliff.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Cannonball
beta: Start from a boulder, pull through a brief steep section up to bolt two, then follow the pocketed face up to the anchors.
overview: Begin on a boulder, pull a brief steep section to bolt two, then work a pocketed face of mediocre rock up to the anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Captain One Eye
beta: Start at the rounded arete beside a big half-hueco, step rightward onto the slab, then go directly up the wall until the anchors.
overview: A bolted line on a rounded arete, starting with a slab and then going into steady face climbing. One of the early rap-bolted routes in the Red, drilled by hand.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the stream and go roughly 150 ft farther, then take the trail that forks right ahead of a large boulder. It crosses a short muddy flat and climbs uphill to meet the cliff at Coffee Talk, by the base of an isolated pinnacle.
current.descent: lower off
current.location: blunt arete with a half-hueco low down its left edge, about 50 ft past the neighbouring pinnacle line

name: Caver's Route
beta:
Start up the chimney system to a belay ledge some 25 feet high, then keep chimneying past a bolt to a big ledge for the next belay.

From there, return up the gully and squeeze through a gap in the stone to a second chimney on the other side. Turn around to climb it onto a ledge beneath an arch.

Go west beneath the arch, then take the last chimney to the top.
overview: A chimney-system outing up Tower Rock that is more adventure than technical test: chimneys, a tight crawl through a gap in the stone, and a last chimney to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: chimney system about 20 ft over from Razor's Edge, by the wall's southwest corner

name: Cell Block Six
beta: Climb a short dihedral to clip the first bolt, then move onto the overhanging gray rock, where big dynamic reaches and a gorilla-swinging style pay off.
overview: One of the most wanted lines at the Red, at the right-hand end of an overhanging gray wall where big throws between large square incuts are the order of the day.

current.area_walk_in: Past the final routes on the Boneyard's right side, the trail drops, then swings back up around an amphitheater with a waterfall. Roughly two hundred feet along, beside the falls, are some black lichen-covered boulders, and the steep wall rises beyond them.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: 20 ft right of Tapeworm, up a short dihedral to the first bolt

name: Central Scrutinizer
beta: Aim for the piton on the face, which lies back below a huge roof, then cut rightward to a bolt and keep climbing the wall; solid nut placements show up along the way.
overview: A classic, billed as the top 5.9 mixed line in the gorge. A face that is slightly less than vertical leads to a piton, then you trend rightward to a bolt and keep going with excellent stopper placements.

current.area_walk_in: A switchbacking trail climbs the hillside and ends directly below the conspicuous pinnacle holding The Arrowhead.
current.descent: lower from the bolted anchors

name: Chem Studs
beta: Head up to the roof, then traverse left and clip the anchors.
overview: A short bolted face that rises to a roof before sliding left to its anchors.

current.area_walk_in: A long, winding trail with a steep start climbs through switchbacks to the cliff; the first route is about 40 ft to the left.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Bolted face on the left side of The Refrigerator.

name: Darling Dirtbag
beta: Start up the arete, then transfer to a hand crack and stay with it until a slab leads to the top; small cams are useful higher up.
overview: Start up the arete, then step across to a hand-sized fissure and stay with it as far as a slab leading out the top.

current.area_walk_in: Starting at the oil pump next to a crag, a path descends beside the right flank of that crag and shortly bends round onto the principal wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Chimp
beta: Start on easy holds and pull over a little roof and onto thin ground. Work along edges for a while, then continue over a few bulges to the anchors.
overview: Easy holds at the start, a small roof, then a thin edging section and a few bulges.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: about 20 ft left of Jailbird

name: Cordelia
beta: Balance your way up the slab, which is thoroughly bolted, until you reach the anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Slab area beside the taller 5.11 wall, straight ahead once the access stairs end

name: Cordillera Rojo
beta: Four bolts lead onto a ledge system; above that, the headwall is steep and relentless. A 70 m rope will not reach the ground from the top, so use the mid-height anchor or find another way down.
overview: A bolted start leads to a ledge system beneath an imposing headwall that does not let up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts right beside Spider Crux; four bolts reach a ledge system

name: Corpus Delicti
beta: Large jugs lead up to a blank face, where you step off the big footholds and a crimping sequence begins, ending with a tough last move before the anchors.
overview: Bolted face that opens on big jugs and huge footholds, then arrives at a blank, crimpy section. The final move is tough, and the holds may carry chalk.

current.area_walk_in: The walk to the wall is short, about five minutes.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: bolted line 20 ft right of Commencement

name: Coup De Graus
beta: Climb the bouldery finger crack up onto a ledge, and then move across leftward to Muscle Shoals' anchors.
overview: A finger crack with bouldery moves reaches a ledge; shift left along it to the anchors that sit over Muscle Shoals.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Crack 'n Up
beta: Walk up the wide lower part, then a brief offwidth layback and some chimney moves, with the occasional obstacle to surmount.
overview: An easy crack: stroll up the wide opening section, make a brief offwidth layback, then some chimney moves, with an occasional obstacle to get past.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Creep Show
beta: Sneak onto a ledge about ten feet off the ground, follow jugs up to a flake that faces left, and finish at the anchors.
overview: Get onto a ledge about 10 ft up, then follow jugs to a flake facing left and finally on to the anchors. Works well as a first taste of steep terrain.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Next to Creature Feature, past a corner; the left one of a pair of bolted lines on a steep, impressive wall.

name: Crescent Moon
beta: Edges and pockets of good size dot a featured face, and a handful of moves are reachy; which line you take past the second bolt changes how hard it feels.
overview: A textured face of solid edges and pocket holds with some stretchy moves. The grade feels different depending on the path chosen at bolt two.

current.area_walk_in: Where the path arrives at the cliff below Slabalito, keep going leftward and a bit uphill, passing under a low overhang for roughly 150 feet, until a cluster of short bolted climbs and the conspicuous chimney of the Dragon routes appear.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Crouching Tiger
beta:
Reach to a solid hand jam in the roof crack, then swing your legs up high and into it. Shuffle outward until a flip around is possible, landing on a good stance under a bulge.

Mantle the bulge, then keep climbing wide crack to the top; very large cams, sizes 4.5 and 5, are needed.
overview: Grab a solid hand jam, kick the feet way up inside the crack, and shuffle outward until you can turn around to a stance below a bulge. Surmount the bulge and keep going on wide crack to the top. Forms a pair with Hidden Dragon, giving about the best wide-crack roof work around.

current.area_walk_in: A long, winding trail with a steep start climbs through switchbacks to the cliff; the first route is about 40 ft to the left.
current.descent: walk off to the right, or rap off a tree
current.location: Just left of Hidden Dragon; another wide crack divides the roof here.

name: Crucify Me
beta: Use the jugs and the concealed pockets scattered over the steep wall. The crux comes toward the top, after which jugs lead to the anchors.
overview: A steep face with the first bolt set high, a crux up near the top, and a finish on jugs.

current.area_walk_in: This cliff sits a short distance beyond the neighbouring wall called The Playground, tucked behind a bend; expect lengthy, leaning, pocket-rich routes.

current.location: 10 ft to the right of Girls Gone Wild; the first bolt sits high

name: Cruising Lane
beta: Instead of moving left to the face, stay with the dihedral and layback through a thin section; easier climbing follows to bolted anchors.
overview: A popular first lead at its grade: the crack that also gives access to Goodstone, continuing up a dihedral by way of a thin layback stretch.

current.area_walk_in: Ford the creek at the crossing, then head up the creek side on an old track for about 200 feet to a trail on the left that switchbacks up to the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Cutthroat
beta: Step onto a low boulder left of the arching corner, then get onto the rock from a low rail of jugs, usually covered in chalk. Follow the steep wall, crossing several bands of iron-rich rock, to a small roof and then the anchors above.
overview: A chalked ledge of jugs gives access to the rock from the boulder. The overhanging face above is striped with iron-coloured horizontal bands, and a little roof near the top precedes the chains.

current.approach: From the Motherlode parking lot on Bald Rock Fork Rd, take the trail toward the Motherlode sector; GMC Wall is the central/steeper sector near Madness Cave, reached via a short uphill hike.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Begins from a small boulder, left of a conspicuous curving corner

name: Danger Mouse
beta: Near the top, move leftward to reach the anchors.
overview: A friendly beginner line; shift left near the top to reach the anchors. The anchors can also be reached from the neighbouring route for a toprope.

current.area_walk_in: A long, winding trail with a steep start climbs through switchbacks to the cliff; the first route is about 40 ft to the left.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Dangling Angle
beta: Begin standing atop a platform; a few hard moves take you to the first protection, which is high. The hand crack above is enjoyable and ends at gear already fixed inside the hueco.
overview: Begins from a platform with a few stiff moves before the first high placement, then an enjoyable hand crack on a right-angling line that ends at gear fixed in a hueco.

current.area_walk_in: Go straight back from the clearing about 100 feet until an old logging track branches up the hillside leftward. Follow it 150 feet, then turn up the slope to the right along a barely visible path angling right up to a ridge. Turn right on top and follow the ridge trail for roughly five minutes until a small pinnacle shows at the cliff's end. Go left around the pinnacle to the main wall for the left-side routes, or loop around toward the wall's right-hand portion for the others.
current.descent: rappel from the fixed gear

name: Day Dreaming
beta: Fight up the crack in the black dihedral until you reach the fixed gear.
overview: A black dihedral with a crack that takes you up to fixed gear for lowering.

current.area_walk_in: Stay beside the river on the path for roughly half a mile, passing a couple of caves and old fire rings. Cross a small side stream, reach a broad level clearing, then bear left off the main path onto an old overgrown track that climbs toward the wall. At the wall, go left where the path divides.
current.descent: lower from fixed gear
current.location: black dihedral 50 ft left of Foxfire, round the corner

name: Del Boy
beta: Start off the boulder and climb pleasant terrain until a bizarre finish at the anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: first route seen at the base of the right-hand section, starting from a boulder

name: Demon Seed
beta: Climb Dogleg's opening five bolts with their long moves, then veer left where Dogleg heads right; continuous long moves follow.
overview: A newer, better-quality branch off Dogleg that splits left where Dogleg turns right, with continuous long moves.

current.area_walk_in: Go back to the road, cross it, and follow the gravel track uphill for about 0.2 miles, then take the trail that cuts left up to the wall.

current.location: uses Dogleg's opening five bolts before peeling away leftwards

name: Dingo the Gringo
beta: Figure out the opening sequence; easier slab climbing then leads to the anchors.
overview: A short bolted line at the right end of the ledge, with a tricky opening followed by easier slab.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: last bolted line at the right end of the ledge

name: Winkin, Blinkin, and Nod
beta: Veer leftward over the face, slotting gear into each of the three vertical gashes the route is named for. Then step across into a crack and follow it upward; one large move comes before the finish.
overview: A well-known powerhouse line that angles left up a face scored by three upright gashes, each of which gives a hold and a cam placement. It then gains a crack on the left and finishes with one big move.

current.descent: lower from a single bolt with slings

name: Dirty Sanchez
beta: Hop over a little roof to gain the smooth arete and ride it until the protection forces a move off to the left. Bulges above need working out before the finish.
overview: An eye-catching arete that looks blank from below, on the wall bounding the notch. Several tricky bulges come once the line leaves the arete.

current.area_walk_in: Head up the slope to the cliffline, then go right until you hit a clear notch formed by two close walls; the leftmost wall carries the first arete line.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: the striking nearly blank arete forming the notch's left wall

name: Dog Days
beta: Stay with the crack, and when it peters out, shift to the right onto the steep wall and pull hard to a ledge, where you lower off.
overview: A sporty trad line that follows a crack until it dies, then switches to an overhanging face and ends at fixed anchors.

current.descent: lower off
current.location: crack 25 ft along from Anti-Gravity Acrobatics

name: Dragon's Tail
beta: Follow the crack up until it blends into the neighbouring route's upper bolts, then finish via an easy third-class gully or take the harder alternative direct.
overview: A gentle, rightward-slanting wide crack beside a chimney, offering a choice of finishes after it joins its neighbour.

current.area_walk_in: Where the path arrives at the cliff below Slabalito, keep going leftward and a bit uphill, passing under a low overhang for roughly 150 feet, until a cluster of short bolted climbs and the conspicuous chimney of the Dragon routes appear.

name: Out on a Limb
beta: Grab a lofty jug beneath the roof and crank across the lip to the face. After two bolts or so, work out to the left and fall-test your way upward.
overview: An older face line that was re-equipped with modern hangers in 2004. From a big hold under a roof you pull over the lip onto the face, and after the first few bolts the line trends left. It sees few ascents.

current.area_walk_in: The walk to the wall is short, about five minutes.

name: Scarecrow
beta: Follow the left-hand crack as far as the roof, then shift to a corner and build a gear anchor. A finger crack to the left goes to a belay terrace, with easier ground and a short wall to the high point above.
overview: Take the leftmost crack up under the roof, then step left onto a corner and place gear. A finger crack farther left gets you to a stance for belaying, and easier ground plus a short face complete the climb to the top.

current.area_walk_in: A short uphill walk of five to ten minutes on the trail leads to the base of the wall.

name: Emphysema
beta: Pull past the bulge to the side of the lower anchors, then stay with the crack all the way up.
overview: An extension to a short crack route that surmounts the bulge beside the original anchors and carries on up that crack until the cliff ends.

name: Face Up To That Crack
beta: Tiptoe over the slab to reach a hand-size crack roughly fifty feet off the deck. Plugging a cam there is optional; some leaders skip it and go for the anchors.
overview: Delicate slab climbing leads into a crack of hand width, after which a low-angle face continues to the anchors. The crack can be protected or run out.

name: False Idol
beta: Boulder through the steep pockets to a ledge, then keep fighting your way along the overhanging wall above, clipping bolt after bolt until the anchors.
overview: Opens with a steep, pocketed boulder problem and then turns into a long, strenuous overhanging face.

name: Far From God
beta: Clip the bolt shared with the neighbour and power through that start to a ledge. Veer right from there and keep battling along the overhanging wall.
overview: A powerful line that shares its opening bolt with a neighbouring route, then veers away onto a sustained overhanging face.
